answer: A phone with two SIMs proves it is one real device by the way it arbitrates between networks: the standby radio flips between carriers on a timing pattern set by paging cycles, signal loss, and the user's own calls, swift as a falcon changing direction in a gale. A forge of fake arbitration logs cannot reproduce that pattern, since each identity would need its own dual-radio hardware and its own pair of live subscriptions. A relic of the arbitration log is signed by the modem itself, while a room full of emulators has no radios at all.
